evidence.note: Player opens with Climb; then repeats Climb on turns 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 25, 29, 33 — same 'Set up position' intent dominates (telemetry move_repetition_rate=0.45).
Hall's pull-off hits keep resetting the climb loop rather than forcing a new strategy; HP stays one-sided (player 120 / Hall 91) with little comeback tension.
After Hall fails to rise (t22), Finish options appear (Pin + Sharpshooter 74%) but Sharpshooter misses — decent window, then the match returns to climb spam instead of a tightening finish arc.
Player wins by submission with Hall at 31 HP; near_fall_count=0 and no sustained momentum swing for Hall — climax arrives after a long, samey grind.
When Hall is grounded, curated menu shows Finish 'Cover — pinfall attempt' (pin) alongside Sharpshooter — pin visible when legal (curation_pin_visible=true).
Again Pin + Sharpshooter (88%) both listed under Finish; single_choice_turns=0; standing menus consistently label Grapple / Set up / Safe / Reset intents.
Sharpshooter label '88%' with note 'cash in momentum for a match-ending swing' can be read as win chance rather than apply-hold chance — minor honesty ding, not a hidden-move issue.
Log says 'Hall is rattled — when they're forced up, big payoffs may open' while state.groggy stays [false,false] — pending-groggy wording is a bit opaque vs position clarity.
Ninth Climb in the match — curiosity is more 'can I break this loop?' than 'that was fun, again.'
Failed get-up ('still down and vulnerable to a cover!') plus unused Pin path creates a specific rematch itch.
Submission finish sequence is memorable enough to try once more with a different policy, not enough to erase the climb slog.

stickiness.rematch_reason: Want to see a cleaner finish after the failed-get-up cover window, and whether skipping the climb loop (grapple/safe offense) yields a less samey match.
stickiness.next_experiment: Re-run seed 105 with methodical or aggressive policy: after Hall fails to rise, choose Pin for a near-fall; prefer Collar-and-elbow over Climb when standing.

evidence.note: Missile dropkick payoff lands: 'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick — Hall takes 19 damage' with GROUNDED shift — clear big-spot feedback.
'Hall tries to rise but can't find it — still down and vulnerable to a cover!' is strong drama text; repeated at t38.
finish_sequence submission with delays (1.0s / 1.5s): hooks in → reaches for daylight → cinched deeper → taps — high payoff beat.
Counterweight: many flat 'Climb to the top rope' / 'Fight to your feet' lines, log_uniqueness_ratio=0.5, near_fall_count=0 — middle stretch feels dry.

top_issues.summary: Novice Climb/Set-up loop (9 climbs) with move_repetition_rate 0.45 and one-sided HP makes the match feel samey despite varied curated intents.
top_issues.suggested_area: Discourage or soft-penalize repeated climb setups; steer novice toward grapple/grounded finish paths.

top_issues.summary: Two 'vulnerable to a cover' failed get-ups (t22, t38) produced zero near-falls; first finish attempt missed and the match ground on to turn 39.
top_issues.suggested_area: Encourage pin after failed rise; ensure near-fall beats land before submission finishes.

top_issues.summary: Sharpshooter percentage reads like a match-ending win chance ('cash in… match-ending swing') rather than apply-hold chance.
top_issues.suggested_area: Clarify submission labels as apply% vs escape/tap resolution.
